clue.text: Rebuked for being carried to work

parts.note: something carried has been taken somewhere
taken as written
a task is a piece of work

explanation.surface: Someone is scolded because they got a lift into the office.
explanation.definitionFit: To be scolded or reprimanded is the idiom's meaning: called to account for a fault.

clue.text: Flavouring is in demand following article

indicators.note: the rest of the wordplay comes after the article, so following places it later

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: in tells us the word is goes inside the word for demand

parts.note: a need is a demand or requirement
taken as written

explanation.surface: A flavour is popular, coming after some newspaper article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demand' looks like the verb, but it is the noun need; the container 'in' gives NISEED, and 'following' means that comes after the article.
explanation.definitionFit: The seed of the anise plant is used as a liquorice-like flavouring in sweets and drinks.

clue.text: Came off a diet for modelling thus!

definitions.text: Came off a diet for modelling thus!

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong or out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A model abandons her diet, and this is how thin she ended up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges CAME and A DIET. The whole clue is also the definition: a dieting model ends up this thin.
explanation.definitionFit: Being very thin and wasted is the state an extreme diet for modelling would leave someone in.

clue.text: Cat and dog ultimately in row

indicators.note: in says the dog's last letter is placed inside the word for row

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so only the final letter of dog is used

explanation.surface: A cat and a dog are squabbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives G, the last letter of dog, and 'in' puts it inside TIER. 'row' reads as a quarrel, but it means a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiger is the largest member of the cat family.

clue.text: The road is up, covering crude depressions

indicators.note: covering means the outer letters wrap around the inner word
in a down clue, up means the letters are read bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a road
rough means crude or unrefined

explanation.surface: Roadworks have dug up the street and left rough potholes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The road is up' reads as roadworks; in a down answer 'is up' turns the street abbreviation into TS, which 'covering' wraps round the crude piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A trough is a long low hollow, as between waves or on a weather chart.

clue.text: Singer discovering mistress in a trance

indicators.note: discovering means uncovering, so the answer is found inside the run of words mistress in a trance

explanation.surface: A singer finds his lover in a dreamy state.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'mistress' through 'in a' into 'trance'.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Sinatra was the American crooner famous for My Way.

clue.text: Rebuke student in associations for napping on floor

parts.note: to carpet someone is to rebuke them, as a boss calling them onto the carpet

indicators.note: in places the student's letter inside the word for associations

parts.note: ties are links or associations
L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A student is told off by his clubs for falling asleep on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'napping' looks like sleeping, but nap is the raised pile on a carpet: these squares give a floor its nap.
explanation.definitionFit: Squares of pile flooring laid side by side give a floor a soft covering with a nap.

clue.text: Porter admits drinking in the morning — a high ball!

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so the word for porter takes the morning letters inside

parts.note: porter is a dark beer
am is the abbreviation for the morning, ante meridiem

explanation.surface: A doorman confesses to drinking before noon, having a ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porter' reads as a doorman, but it is a dark beer. In cricket a beamer is a ball bowled at head height without bouncing.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, a beamer is a full toss bowled at head height without bouncing.

clue.text: Country dancing a crime before midday?

indicators.note: before puts the shuffled letters ahead of the last piece
dancing letters move about, so the words a crime are rearranged

parts.note: read as mid day, the middle letter of the word day

explanation.surface: Someone commits a crime of dancing before noon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'midday' is split as 'mid day': the middle letter of 'day'. 'dancing' rearranges A CRIME into AMERIC, and 'before' puts that ahead of the A.
explanation.definitionFit: The United States is commonly called by this name, a nation in North America.

clue.text: Good horses generate complaints

parts.note: roans are horses with a coat flecked with white

explanation.surface: Fine horses cause people to grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Moans and grumbles are expressions of complaint.

clue.text: One culpable by self-admission

parts.note: reads as someone who confesses guilt, but the admission is letting oneself into a party uninvited

explanation.surface: A person who owns up to their own guilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'self-admission' suggests confessing, but here it means admitting yourself to an event without an invitation.
explanation.definitionFit: An uninvited guest who lets themselves into a party is guilty by their own entry.

clue.text: Old city ceremony that's turned one

parts.note: pomp is splendid ceremony

indicators.note: turned means the letters are turned round and read backwards

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation for id est, that is
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An ancient city where a ceremony has changed one person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' stands for 'that is', i.e. IE, which 'turned' reverses to EI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman town near Naples was buried by Vesuvius in AD 79.

clue.text: Set a target for races at Henley

indicators.note: set means arranged or fixed in place, so the letters of a target are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Organisers fix a goal for the rowing races on the Thames.
explanation.walkthrough: Henley-on-Thames hosts the Royal Regatta, a famous rowing event in England.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowing event made up of a series of boat races, Henley's being the best known.

clue.text: Bound to come across resistance, though exhausted

indicators.note: coming across something means meeting it on the way, so the word for bound takes the letter for resistance inside

parts.note: tied means bound with rope
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Someone is sure to meet opposition, yet is too weary to fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' reads as 'certain', but it means tied up.
explanation.definitionFit: Being worn out and needing rest is the plain meaning of both.

clue.text: He merits a shabby multiple occupancy property

indicators.note: shabby means worn and out of shape, so the letters of he merits a are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man deserves a run-down holiday flat shared with others.
explanation.definitionFit: A holiday home owned jointly, each owner using it for set weeks of the year.

clue.text: Italian family sourcing nuts and leaves of health-giving properties

parts.note: the Medici were the ruling family of Renaissance Florence

indicators.note: sourcing points to where each word starts, so the first letter of each is taken

explanation.surface: An Italian family obtains nuts and leaves for their healing powers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sourcing' takes the first letters of 'nuts', 'and' and 'leaves': NAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Having healing or curative value, like a remedy.

clue.text: I am beaten but restrained

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am
pounded means beaten hard

explanation.surface: Someone is beaten up yet held back.
explanation.definitionFit: Seized and held in custody, as goods or a stray animal are confined.

clue.text: Rifle of convict buried in mound

indicators.note: buried in means placed deep inside, so the convict word goes within the mound word

parts.note: a pile is a heap or mound
a lag is slang for a convict

explanation.surface: A prisoner's gun is hidden under a heap of earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rifle' reads as a gun, but here it is a verb meaning to ransack.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle is to ransack or plunder, as robbers do.

clue.text: Centre court member under twenty? Lots of them

parts.note: an umpire, ump for short, is an official on Wimbledon's Centre Court
a teen is someone aged under twenty

explanation.surface: A young tennis player on Centre Court, one of many.
explanation.walkthrough: Centre Court is Wimbledon's main tennis court; the official there is the umpire.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial word for an indefinitely large number, very many.

clue.text: Locks put on key seat

indicators.note: put on means placed after, in an across answer

parts.note: C is a musical key
locks are tresses of hair

explanation.surface: Hair is laid on a key part of the seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locks' and 'key' suggest a door, but locks are hair and C is a key in music.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of furniture for one person to sit on.

clue.text: Look into jazz group from island capital

indicators.note: into places the word for look inside the jazz group

parts.note: a combo is a small jazz band
lo is an old word for look, as in lo and behold

explanation.surface: Checking out a jazz band from an island city.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief city and former capital of Sri Lanka, an island nation.

clue.text: The sum paid for a horse

parts.note: a mount is a horse that is ridden

explanation.surface: The price paid for a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A total quantity or sum of money.

clue.text: Obscure English crocodile, perhaps outwardly savage

parts.note: a crocodile clip is one kind of clip, so crocodile is an example

indicators.note: outwardly means on the outside, so only the first and last letters of savage are taken

explanation.surface: An obscure English crocodile seems fierce on the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crocodile' is a crocodile clip, a spring clip with toothed jaws. 'outwardly' takes the first and last letters of savage, SE.
explanation.definitionFit: To block out or overshadow, as the moon hides the sun.

clue.text: Sex spread across the morning papers!

indicators.note: across means stretched over, so the rearranged letters surround the morning abbreviation
spread means scattered, so the letters of sex are rearranged

parts.note: am is the abbreviation for the morning

explanation.surface: Sex scandals splashed across the morning newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' shuffles the first word into EXS, and 'across' stretches that over the morning abbreviation. 'papers' looks like newspapers, but means test papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Test papers sat by students are what pupils face at the end of term.

clue.text: Insensitive opposition leader follows visit to America

indicators.note: follows means the opposition letter comes after the visit word

parts.note: to call is to pay a visit

indicators.note: leader means the first letter, the one at the front, of opposition

parts.note: US is the abbreviation for the United States of America

explanation.surface: An unfeeling opposition leader trails a trip to the States.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard-hearted and unfeeling, with no sympathy for others.

clue.text: One shoots with English gunner on university river

indicators.note: on means placed after, in an across answer

parts.note: the Cam flows through Cambridge, a university city
RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners

explanation.surface: Someone fires a gun alongside an English gunner on the river at Cambridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shoots' reads as firing a gun, but this one shoots pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: A photographer shoots pictures with this device.

clue.text: Candidate's refusal — explosive energy

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, linking the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: no is a refusal
a mine is an explosive device
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A candidate says no to a bomb with energy.
explanation.definitionFit: A person put forward for a post or award is a candidate.

clue.text: Wine snob let drunk suffer with this affliction

indicators.note: drunk means tipsy and disordered, so the letters of wine snob let are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wine snob who drinks too much will suffer this ailment.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a drinker's hangover, but the ailment is a sports strain of the forearm tendons.
explanation.definitionFit: A painful inflammation of the tendons of the outer elbow caused by overuse.
